turns.content: Label the vertices of the regular 2006-gon cyclically. Characterize an odd side or diagonal by the parity of the number of boundary edges between its endpoints.
For an isosceles triangle whose two equal sides are odd, explain how the two corresponding boundary arcs constrain the placement of its apex and base.
Use Euler's formula for the total number of triangles in a triangulation as the sole method for bounding the number of isosceles triangles with two odd sides.
Using the induction setup and candidate bound, split the subpolygon along the selected longest-base triangle and account for the resulting boundary pieces.
Apply the lemma to a longest dissecting diagonal XY and its adjacent triangle XYZ to obtain an upper bound for the entire triangulation.
Give a triangulation that attains the bound established above, describe its core vertex-joining rule, and count the qualifying triangles after the remaining regions are completed.
Combine the upper bound and construction to determine the maximum possible number.
